open_decisions.title: The capability CTE is still written three times
open_decisions.authority: Round-15 architecture finding A15-1 (ADR-133)
open_decisions.note: AMENDED 2026-08-06 (round 19, finding R19-CTR-2). THE ORIGINAL NOTE'S BASIS WAS FALSE. It read 'the round-15 battery makes the three copies provably agree -- any drift fails seven cases at the drifting write -- so this is a duplication, not a live risk'. MEASURED: replacing `ra.account_id = $n::uuid` with a same-arity tautology left all 27 battery examples green, and across the whole 2464-example suite the only thing that reacted was `repository_truth_spec`'s mutation-applicability check -- a byte-digest staleness test that produces the IDENTICAL failure for a comment-only edit. Nothing in the suite could distinguish deleting an authorization qual from adding a comment. Six single-qual drifts were tried; only `FOR SHARE OF ra` was caught. REPAIRED IN PART: round 19 added a shared-example case binding the PRINCIPAL conjunct at all three writes (verified to fail at exactly the drifting write, independently at each), and ledger definition `r19-account-qual-unbound`. WHAT REMAINS: the organization limb is still unproved, and R19-ARCH-3 showed the copies agree in SQL TEXT while ALREADY DIFFERING in the operand bound to the organization slot -- `crawl_store`/`crawl_policy_store` bind the ROW's id, `crawl_start_store` binds the AUTHORITY's -- which a textual comparison cannot see. The architecture lens's reasoned verdict is that EXTRACTION IS THE WRONG REPAIR: the predicate is safe because it is a conjunct of the statement with nothing to hoist, and a shared fragment interpolated into three statements moves back toward the rule-split-across-writers shape ADR-095 records. The right repair is one architecture spec asserting the three CTEs are equivalent under placeholder normalisation AND that each binds the same semantic value into the organization slot. ROUND-20 MEASUREMENT (finding F-3), which sharpens what remains: a per-qual attribution matrix of 30 same-arity tautologies (10 conjuncts x 3 writes) shows every conjunct killing the same named example at each write — no case is vacuous at one write while meaningful at another. TWO CONJUNCTS KILL NOTHING IN THE BATTERY. `required_role` at the policy write is bound outside it (PROOF 258) and is genuinely inert at the other two, where production passes none. `ra.organization_id` IS UNBOUND ACROSS THE ENTIRE 2472-EXAMPLE SUITE at all three writes — the only reaction is `repository_truth_spec`'s byte-digest staleness check, which fires identically for a comment-only edit. That is the organization limb this note already records as unproved, now measured against the whole suite rather than the battery alone.

open_decisions.title: ProtectedEffectDoor's 42601 branch records nothing
open_decisions.authority: Round-15 schema observation O-3 (ADR-133)
open_decisions.note: AMENDED 2026-08-06 (round 19, findings R19-SCHEMA-2 and R19-SCHEMA-3). THE STATED JUSTIFICATION IS FALSE, THOUGH THE CONCLUSION STILL HOLDS. The door's comment says a 42601 statement 'carries no ModifyTable, so the absence of a plan is the correct answer rather than a blind spot'. `EXPLAIN` accepts only `ExplainableStmt`, and several statements outside that production DO modify tables. Reproduced through the door's own plan path: TRUNCATE, `COPY ... FROM STDIN`, CALL and `DO $$..$$` are all SWALLOWED_AS_NO_WRITE, and the COPY case demonstrably wrote 2 rows while the door returned []. A sweep of app/ and lib/ finds zero such production statements, so the corpus conclusion stands and this is NON-BLOCKING. SECOND INSTANCE, SAME CLASS, AND THIS ONE HAS A LIVE CALL SITE (R19-SCHEMA-3): the door is equally blind to DML inside SECURITY DEFINER plpgsql. Fifteen volatile SECURITY DEFINER functions perform DML and `f1_settle_scheduled_action` is called from `record_fetch_attempt.rb`; not exploitable against AuthoritySentinel because that path is a service delivery so the human-authorized antecedent is false. REPAIR: stop inferring 'no write' from the absence of a plan. `GovernedWriteSentinel` already holds the executed `PG::Result`, and PostgreSQL's own command tag (`cmd_status` -> 'COPY 2', 'TRUNCATE TABLE', 'MERGE ...') answers 'did this modify a relation' without a regex.

open_decisions.title: The write's capability limb is a grant-identity limb, not a capability limb
open_decisions.authority: Round-15 security observation O1 (ADR-133)
open_decisions.note: WriteAuthority#capability is compared in Ruby by same_principal? and is bound into no statement. The SQL asks whether the grant the decision named is still the grant it named; it does not ask whether that grant CONFERS the capability. With the baseline confers? check neutralised (base code, out of range) a SecurityOperator queued and cancelled a Crawl; ActivateCrawlPolicy survived only because required_role gives that one write a role axis. Repair consistent with ADR-132's no-second-copy ruling: derive a required-role set from the single Ruby transcription and pass it for all three capabilities as SCOPE_ROLE already is. RESOLVED 2026-08-06 by ADR-135 (round-17 finding R17-SEC-1): `WriteAuthority` now carries `allowed_roles` — the ratified PermissionBaseline cell, read once in Ruby, immutable for the life of a deploy — and every protected write binds `AND ra.canonical_role = ANY($n::text[])`. The battery gains the case at all three writes and three mutations bind it.

open_decisions.title: Two protected writes judge authority against the row's organization_id, the third against the authority's
open_decisions.authority: Round-16 security observation O2 (ADR-134)
open_decisions.note: AMENDED 2026-08-06 (round 19, findings R19-SEC-4 and R19-SCHEMA-1). MEASURED FROM BOTH SIDES, and the divergence is real in both directions while the composite fails closed. SECURITY LENS: `crawl_start_store#cancel` binds both CTEs to `authority.organization_id` while its `UPDATE crawls ... WHERE id = $1::uuid` carries NO organization predicate; driven with a real attacker session against a victim organization's running Crawl, BOTH authority limbs returned authorized (`epoch_authorized: true, capability_authorized: true`) and only RLS stopped the write (`moved: 0`). SCHEMA LENS: the mirror in `crawl_store#insert_crawl`, which binds the ROW's org -- an org-B authority against an org-A row returned `epoch_authorized: true`, failing closed only via the capability CTE, and `role_assignments` has NO foreign keys at all, so that consistency is a WF-013 guarantee rather than a database one. UNREACHABLE from any built handler: `queue_crawl.rb`, `activate_crawl_policy.rb` and `cancel_crawl.rb` all derive org from the authenticated actor. NON-BLOCKING. The repair is still the one recorded: bind all three to the AUTHORITY's organization and add `AND organization_id = $n::uuid` to cancel's UPDATE target, so each store holds its own contract rather than depending on the one caller that derives the id correctly -- which is the principle `crawl_policy_store.rb:135` already ratified.

open_decisions.title: OWNER DECISION REQUIRED: `PROTECTED` omits three permissions the ratified `:333` enumeration names, and one is a live authorization bypass
open_decisions.authority: Round-19 finding R19-SEC-2 / R19-ARCH-2 / R19-CTR-5 (ADR-137). Expressly NOT taken under S-07-009 repair authority.
open_decisions.note: REPRODUCED THREE TIMES INDEPENDENTLY, through the real handler, with controls. `WORKFLOW_SPECIFICATIONS.md:333` is the ratified authority for which grants are protected (':335 This enumeration is the authority'). It names 18; `Platform::PermissionBaseline::PROTECTED` has 15. Absent: `policy.entitlement.manage`, `security.investigation.approve`, and the SecurityOperator `organization.close` arm. TWO ARE HARMLESS -- SecurityOperator is already protected through other keys, so both are under-grants in the fail-closed direction and affect only the exactness of `:240`'s preview. THE THIRD IS NOT. `:175` makes BillingOperator the ONLY role whose `policy.entitlement.manage` cell reads `allow`, and BillingOperator appears in no other PROTECTED entry, so `protected_role?('BillingOperator')` is false. `request_role_assignment.rb:61` therefore classes the request non-protected, `GrantAuthority.evaluate` is called with `direct: true`, and `grant_authority.rb:52`'s `invitation_approval_required` refusal never fires. MEASURED: RequestRoleAssignment for BillingOperator driven by a seeded OrganizationAdmin returns success=true and lands status=active, expires_at=nil, approval_due_at=nil, zero approval records, allowlist=[]. The SecurityOperator control on the same path returns success=false / role_expiry_required. `:333`/`:314`/`:316` require approval within 24 hours by a SecurityOperator OTHER than the requester and a mandatory active expiry no later than 30 days; `:140` confines an OrganizationAdmin's `role.manage` cell to 'non-protected tenant grants'. So a single OrganizationAdmin, acting alone, issues an immediately-active never-expiring grant carrying protected authority. NO PROOF ASSERTS THE WRONG STATE AND NONE WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: `permission_baseline_transcription_spec.rb` checks CAPABILITIES against `:135` in two dimensions and has NO check of PROTECTED against `:333`. WHY THIS IS AN OWNER DECISION AND NOT A REPAIR. It is outside `b2e8cfb..dd78732`, it is pre-existing, it blocks no mandatory gate (all pass), and it belongs to accepted WF-013 work. AUTONOMY_POLICY's blocking-defect repair authority ends: 'This is not permission to work on another tranche's backlog, nor to repair defects that are not blocking a mandatory gate.' The fix also CHANGES THE BEHAVIOUR OF AN ACCEPTED TRANCHE -- BillingOperator grants would begin requiring SecurityOperator approval and a mandatory expiry. Precedent: the round-2 `:442` violation ('it needs a follow-up of its own and an owner decision; this review opens neither') and ADR-131. IT DOES NOT BLOCK S-07-009: it makes no crawl capability protected, so the round-19 finding that the protected-grant conjunct is vacuous for `crawl.trigger`/`crawl.cancel`/`policy.crawl.manage` is unaffected, and BillingOperator's `:147`/`:173` cells read `deny` so the write-level `ra.canonical_role = ANY(allowed_roles)` predicate refuses it at all three WF-005 writes regardless. RECOMMENDED REPAIR when authorised: add all three entries (`organization.close` mapped to SecurityOperator ONLY, since `:333` expressly exempts the OrganizationAdmin request arm), and add a THIRD DIMENSION to `permission_baseline_transcription_spec.rb` deriving PROTECTED from the `:333` sentence the way it already derives CAPABILITIES from the `:135` table. CAUTION the repair must handle: `protected_grant?` is ROLE-BLIND, so once `organization.close` is materialized it would demand the permission in an OrganizationAdmin's allowlist too, which `:333` says it must not. Inert today because `organization.close` is not in CAPABILITIES, but the gate needs the role arm before that capability is materialized. ROUND-20 CORROBORATION (finding F6), through a SECOND handler and with the vacuity measured in the other direction. `CreateInvitation` for BillingOperator returns success with `state="active"`, `approval_due_at=nil` and preview `[]`, emitting `InvitationActivated`; the SecurityOperator control goes `pending_approval` / `InvitationApprovalRequested`. Adding `"policy.entitlement.manage" => %w[BillingOperator]` flips it to `pending_approval` with preview `["policy.entitlement.manage"]` and breaks nothing else. AND THE TABLE IS UNBOUND ENTRY BY ENTRY: DELETING the ratified entry `policy.export.manage` from `PROTECTED` leaves the FULL SUITE at 2472 examples, 0 failures — no example and no digest check reacts. So the recorded repair MUST include the third `permission_baseline_transcription_spec` dimension (PROTECTED derived from the `:333` sentence). Without it the fix would land with nothing keeping it correct, which is how the omission survived in the first place.

open_decisions.title: `write_observer_spec` does not exercise the production hook it claims to prove, and `GovernedWriteSentinel` has no suite-end non-vacuity check
open_decisions.authority: Round-19 architecture finding R19-ARCH-1 (ADR-137)
open_decisions.note: Eight of the file's ten examples build their own anonymous module and stand-in base class and never touch `GovernedWriteSentinel::Instrumentation`. MEASURED: replacing the production `Instrumentation#exec_params` body with a bare `super` -- so it observes nothing -- leaves `spec/architecture/write_observer_spec.rb` at 10 examples, 0 failures. NON-BLOCKING because the instrument IS bound: the same gutted hook fails `spec/acceptance/wf005_closed_fact_set_spec.rb` 7/7, and `complete_test_suite` is a mandatory manifest gate. What is wrong is the gate file's own header, which claims to be what binds it. SECOND HALF, AND THE MORE IMPORTANT ONE: unlike `AuthoritySentinel.assert_observed!`, `GovernedWriteSentinel` has NO `after(:suite)` non-vacuity check, so blinding it makes the run GREENER rather than failing it. REPAIR: point at least one example at `PG::Connection` with `Instrumentation` prepended, and add a suite-end `census.empty? -> raise` guard mirroring `assert_observed!`.

open_decisions.title: `RaceHarness.open_connection` opens a raw unbounded connection, contradicting `PgTestConnection`'s own docstring
open_decisions.authority: Round-19 concurrency finding R19-CONC-6 (ADR-137)
open_decisions.note: MEASURED: `DbInspector` connections carry `statement_timeout = 15s`; `RaceHarness.open_connection` (`spec/support/race_harness.rb:196`) uses a bare `PG.connect` and carries `statement_timeout = 0`. That is the exact defect `spec/support/pg_test_connection.rb` was written to remove, and its docstring's claim to be 'the one place the suite opens a RAW PostgreSQL connection' is false. Three waits in `wf005_authority_lock_order_spec.rb` run on these connections with no bound of any kind (`pg_advisory_lock` at :130, `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` at :276 and :563). NON-BLOCKING: each contends only with rows its own example just created, and no hang could be demonstrated. REPAIR: `RaceHarness.open_connection` should route through `PgTestConnection.connect(user: DbInspector.superuser)`. RELATED AND NOW CLOSED: the 'deliberately unbounded' lock-order probe setup that BUILD_STATE carried as live exposure is in fact bounded by the 15s `statement_timeout` -- measured at 17.28s to `PG::QueryCanceled` with a complete residue report. It degrades to a failing example, never a hang, and is NOT a stability violation.

open_decisions.title: PROOF 264 measures the lock order at one of the three protected writes
open_decisions.authority: Round-19 concurrency finding R19-CONC-1 (ADR-137)
open_decisions.note: PROOF 264 drives only `QueueCrawl`, and `blocks_on_held_grant?` only drives `CrawlStore#insert_crawl`. The order at `cancel` and `activate_version` is ASSUMED -- this tranche's own declared defect class, and the one round 16 was called for. The concurrency lens measured all three from both ends with `pg_blocking_pids` and the order HOLDS everywhere, so this is NON-BLOCKING. But it holds as a property of the PLANNER (materialized-CTE / InitPlan evaluation order), not of anything enforced, and in `crawl_policy_store.rb:120` the two EXISTS sit in one CTE where `order_qual_clauses` sorts by estimated cost. REPAIR: run PROOF 264's measurement at all three writes using the `WRITES` battery shape `wf005_grant_battery_spec.rb` already establishes.

open_decisions.title: The protected-grant limb has NO counterpart at any protected write, and the safety of that is a caller census
open_decisions.authority: Round-19 adversarial finding R-ADV-1 (ADR-138)
open_decisions.note: The three protected writes never read `protected_permission_allowlist` or `bootstrap_admin_exception` for ANY capability. `confers?`'s `return true unless PROTECTED.key?` is a property of the RUBY evaluator and has no analogue in the SQL, so the stores' comment 'this is the baseline CARRIED' is inaccurate: what is carried is the baseline MINUS its protected limb. MEASURED at `CrawlStartStore#cancel` with an ordinary OrganizationAdmin grant and capability `role.manage`: Ruby `authorize` DENIES (`missing_authority`, granting=0) while the write returns `capability_authorized=true, moved=1` and irreversibly cancels a running Crawl. LATENT, not live: no production caller passes a protected capability to these writes, and `CAPABILITIES.fetch` raises KeyError for 13 of the 15 PROTECTED keys, so the exposed surface is exactly `role.manage` and `invitation.approve` — the two keys in both tables. BUT the safety rests on a CALLER CENSUS, which is the 'one deletion away from nothing' shape FU-48 exists to remove, and the census is wider than recorded: `WriteAuthority.for` has FOUR call sites in app/, not three — the three handlers plus `app/workflows/wf005/authority_attestation.rb:66`, reached through `PostWaitDecision#authority_attestation`. Both `attest` and `authority_attestation` take a free `capability:` parameter. REPAIR OPTIONS: carry a `protected_permitted` boolean derived from `PROTECTED.key?(capability)` the way `read_only_permitted` already carries the sixth column, with the allowlist bound when it is true; or refuse at the builder — `WriteAuthority.for` raises for a capability in PROTECTED until the limb is carried, which turns the census into an enforced invariant. The second is smaller and fails closed.

open_decisions.title: `f1_role_assignments_lifecycle_guard` is BEFORE UPDATE only; an INSERT may mint an active grant with any protected allowlist
open_decisions.authority: Round-19 adversarial finding R-ADV-3 (ADR-138)
open_decisions.note: The only trigger on `role_assignments` is `role_assignments_lifecycle_guard BEFORE UPDATE FOR EACH ROW`. There is NO INSERT trigger and NO DELETE trigger, and the only CHECK touching the allowlist for a non-pending row is the 30-day expiry rule (`role_assignment_pending_has_no_allowlist` is `status <> 'pending' OR ...`). So an INSERT may create a row with `status='active'`, any allowlist including all 15 PROTECTED keys, and `bootstrap_admin_exception=true`, bounded only by `bootstrap_exception_is_admin` and the one-per-org partial unique index. `RoleAssignmentStore#insert` takes both as free parameters and its sole caller hardcodes `[]`. CONTAINED TODAY: `f1_runtime` holds INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE but NOT DELETE, and no `f1_*` role is superuser or bypassrls, so delete-and-reinsert, `session_replication_role` and `DISABLE TRIGGER` are all unavailable. DOES NOT REACH THE PROTECTED WRITES: an INSERT mints a new id and the capability CTE joins on the CARRIED `g.id = ra.id AND g.state_version = ra.state_version`; the `pending -> active` route cannot apply either, because `effective_role_assignments` selects `status='active'` only and the transition bumps `state_version`. WHY IT IS RECORDED ANYWAY: round 19 cited this guard as an INDEPENDENT ground for the safety of the unbound protected limb, and it is not one — dual control at INSERT time is enforced in Ruby alone. REPAIR: extend the guard to BEFORE INSERT for the allowlist and bootstrap columns, or add a CHECK that an inserted active row carries an empty allowlist unless the bootstrap exception applies.

open_decisions.title: `AuthorityFixture` carries second copies of BOTH write-authority derivations, and nothing binds them to the production builder
open_decisions.authority: Round-19 final-gate adversarial finding A-1 (ADR-138)
open_decisions.note: `spec/support/authority_fixture.rb:31-32` computes `CAPABILITIES.fetch(capability)` and `READ_ONLY_CAPABILITIES.include?(capability)` independently of `IdentityAccess::Authorization::WriteAuthority.for`. THIS IS THE MECHANISM THAT HID R-ADV-2: because every battery case built its authority through the fixture, all of them proved what the STATEMENT does with a correct value and none proved the value was derived, which is how three capability-scoped mutations survived 1185 acceptance examples. The round-19 repair routes the two new cases around the fixture via `production_authority`, so the LIVE gap is closed, but the duplicate expressions remain and NOTHING ASSERTS THEY AGREE — `grep -rn AuthorityFixture spec/architecture/` returns nothing. They are textually identical today, so there is no live divergence; the exposure is future drift. If `WriteAuthority.for` gains a third input or changes a derivation, every fixture-built case keeps proving the old shape while production uses the new one, silently. REPAIR: the fixture's DEFAULTS should come from the production builder, with explicit overrides retained for the deliberately-wrong authorities the negative proofs need (that capability is the fixture's stated purpose and must not be removed). A one-example architecture gate asserting that `AuthorityFixture.build` with no overrides equals `WriteAuthority.for` on `allowed_roles` and `read_only_permitted` for EVERY materialized capability would convert the assumption into a control, in the shape `permission_baseline_transcription_spec.rb` already establishes. MEASURED at round 20 (finding F-4), both directions, one capability at a time: breaking the PRODUCTION derivation dies at exactly the affected write for all SIX capability/expression pairs (ADR-138 verified three of the six; the other three also hold). In the fixture direction, a permissive drift of its `read_only_permitted` copy fails LOUD (3 failures, one per write), while a permissive drift of its `allowed_roles` copy changes NO verdict — it is invisible and simultaneously load-bearing for nothing, because the one case needing a restrictive cell passes `allowed_roles: %w[NoSuchRole]` explicitly and a union still contains the actor's role so the COMMIT control still commits. So the duplication CANNOT be made to hide a real defect today; the exposure is purely future drift, in a case written later against the fixture default. ROUND-20 EXTENSION (finding F4): the fixture diverges from production in SELECTION as well as in derivation, which this note did not record. `AuthorityFixture.active_grants` selects a WIDER set than `AuthorizationStore#effective_role_assignments` — measured 1 row vs 0 for an active-but-not-yet-effective grant — and applies no `confers?` filter at all. It also orders `grant_ids` by `ORDER BY id` while production takes whatever order `effective_role_assignments` returns, which carries NO `ORDER BY`; `same_principal?` compares those arrays with `==`. Neither is reachable, because a write's authority and its attestation are built from the same `Decision` object, but a fixture that selects differently from production is the same hazard class as one that derives differently, and the repair should cover both.

open_decisions.title: Nothing enforces the completeness of the battery's `WRITES` set, on which the round-19 repair's structural claim depends
open_decisions.authority: Round-19 final-gate adversarial finding A-2 (ADR-138)
open_decisions.note: `spec/acceptance/wf005_grant_battery_spec.rb:56` declares `WRITES` as a hand-maintained literal, and the only thing referencing it is the `WRITES.each` at :447. The round-19 repair's claim to be STRUCTURAL rather than three more proofs rests entirely on inheritance: twelve shared examples run at every entry in that map. A FOURTH PROTECTED WRITE WOULD INHERIT NONE OF THEM and no gate would say so. Completeness was established this round by the architecture lens planning all 391 SQL statements in app/ and lib/ through `EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN)` and collecting `ModifyTable` nodes — exactly six statements modify `crawls`/`crawl_policies`, the three human-authorized ones carry `WriteAuthority` and the three service ones (`start`, `fail`, `terminalize`) have no human path because neither caller ever calls `authenticate`. But that was a REVIEW ACTIVITY, not a gate, and it does not run again. REPAIR: an architecture spec that derives the protected-write set from the repository as EVERY STATEMENT CARRYING A `capability_authority` CTE, and fails when it is not exactly the set `WRITES` enumerates. AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS NOTE ALSO OFFERED 'every store method taking an `authority:` parameter', AND THAT DERIVATION IS WRONG: measured, only `CrawlStartStore#cancel` takes it as a keyword; `insert_crawl` and `activate_version` receive it inside a row Hash via `row.fetch(:authority)`, and a `[:authority]` grep additionally matches an unrelated WF-013 ledger column at `role_assignment_store.rb:131`. A gate written to that spec would cover 1 of 3 and PASS — this tranche's own defect class inside the repair for it. The CTE derivation is exact repo-wide: 3 of 3, zero false positives, and `epoch_authority` cross-checks to the same set. That removes the class rather than the instance, which is the standard ADR-095 and the round-15 A15-1 repair both set. PRIORITY, MEASURED: `crawl.recover` is ratified in WORKFLOW_SPECIFICATIONS.md's WF-005 Recovery Path and is NOT in `PermissionBaseline::CAPABILITIES`, so a fourth protected write is SCHEDULED WORK rather than a hypothesis, and the gate should exist before it lands.

open_decisions.title: `ReactivateOrganization` consults the Permission Baseline through a ONE-LIMB path, outside `CommandAuthorizer`
open_decisions.authority: Round-20 authority-consistency finding F5
open_decisions.note: `Platform::PermissionBaseline.permits?` has exactly two callers. `CommandAuthorizer#confers?` applies three limbs — role cell, `permission_mode`, protected allowlist. `app/workflows/wf013/handlers/reactivate_organization.rb:100` applies ONLY THE ROLE LIMB, and `OrganizationLifecycleStore#effective_role_assignments` does not even SELECT `permission_mode`. That is R3-10's exact shape — the sixth column dropped because the caller reads a role-keyed table — surviving OUTSIDE the class that was repaired. UNREACHABLE TODAY, by two independent facts: `organization.reactivate`'s only non-deny canonical role is OrganizationAdmin, and OrganizationAdmin + `read_only` is not a ratified tuple (`:314`). But the tuple is barred by `InvitationOffer.valid_tuple?` at the three creation paths and by NOTHING IN THE DATABASE — which is FU-59's observation arriving from a second direction. PRE-EXISTING and untouched by `b2e8cfb..07f1471`; does not block S-07-009. Recorded because it is precisely the class this tranche exists to remove: an authorization control implemented once properly and once partially, with only the caller set keeping the partial one safe. REPAIR: route it through `CommandAuthorizer`, or have `permits?` refuse to answer without the mode it needs.

open_decisions.title: BLOCKING FOR S-07-009: five authorization controls in the WF-005 write path are proved at one instance and assumed at the others
open_decisions.authority: Round-20 universal-vs-instance findings R20-1..R20-5
open_decisions.note: 78 narrowly-scoped, arity-preserving mutations; 48 survived; 5 confirmed against the FULL 1191-example acceptance corpus. NOT A PRODUCT DEFECT: 12 probes driving the real stores and real handlers all pass at HEAD, and no reachable bypass was found on any axis. These are EVIDENCE gaps, the same category ADR-138 recorded. R20-1 `g.id = ra.id` IS BOUND BY NOTHING at all three writes; unbinding it at the queue write survives the full corpus, and driven at the store it QUEUES A CRAWL ON A REVOKED GRANT. Verified centrally: with the conjunct unbound the battery is 36 examples / 0 failures. The R19-CTR-2 foreign-account case does NOT bind it — `TenantSeeder` inserts state_version 0 with NULL scope while the bootstrap grant is state_version 1 with a scope digest, so that case is discriminated by the VERSION and SCOPE conjuncts and never reaches identity. Two grants at the same version is a PRODUCTION shape (`invitation_store.rb:113` creates active grants at state_version 0). This also undermines FU-59's containment argument, which rests on `g.id`. R20-2 the `WriteAuthority.for` derivations are bound only against the two roles and the one mode-tuple the battery seeds. Surviving the full corpus: widening `allowed_roles` by `SecurityOperator` (a role `:147` denies outright) — driven, it cancels a Crawl; deriving `read_only_permitted` as `!required_role.nil?` — driven, A READ-ONLY EXECUTIVE BUYER ACTIVATES AN IMMUTABLE PROJECT-SCOPE CRAWL POLICY; and dropping `required_role` for PROJECT scope alone. Root cause: THE ENTIRE PROJECT-SCOPE CONFIGURATION OF `ActivateCrawlPolicy` HAS NO WRITE-LEVEL NEGATIVE PROOF — every existing driver uses organization scope with `required_role: nil`. R20-3 `same_principal?` binds 1 of its 10 members (only `capability`, via PROOF 251). R20-4 'refused BEFORE the lock' is proved only for an actor holding NO Assignment; with the baseline-cell conjunct neutralised a TechnicalImplementer TAKES THE LOCK before refusal, which is the PRULE-039 / SEC-REQ-005 property. R20-5 `ra.status = 'active'` is bound only against `revoked`; admitting `pending` survives at all three writes, and that distinction is the premise of ADR-133's R15-CONC-1 deadlock-freedom exemption. REPAIR, structural, in the shape `permission_baseline_transcription_spec.rb` already establishes: (1) derive the battery's negative population from the ratified `:135` table — for each write, every canonical role whose cell reads `deny` — instead of hand-picking one role; (2) parameterise `WRITES` with each write's PRODUCTION `required_role` and add a PROJECT-scope entry for the policy write; (3) add a case where the carried grant id names a revoked Assignment while a live sibling of the same principal exists at the same version and scope; (4) drive `require!` over `WriteAuthority.members` so a new member is covered by construction; (5) drive PROOF 255/256/257 with a denied-ROLE actor as well as a no-assignment one; (6) move one status case from `revoked` to `pending`.
